summary: Kay Koppedrayer is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. She studied at McGill University (BA) and McMaster University (MA), and is attested as retired from Wilfrid Laurier University in 2005.

Kazi Dawa Samdup (1868–1922) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Bhutia Boarding School under Ugyen Gyatso and with Tshampa Norbu. He served as headmaster at Bhutia Boarding School (~1906–1919) and lecturer at the University of Calcutta (1920).

Kazu Uehara (1924–2017) worked in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He completed coursework at Kyushu University and served as a full-time lecturer at the University of Miyazaki and professor emeritus at Seijo University (~1968–1995).

Kazuaki Komine (b. 1947) specializes in Japanology and Buddhist studies. Educated at Waseda University, he held posts at Waseda Jitsugyo High School (1974), Tokushima University (1979), the National Institute of Japanese Literature (1984), and Rikkyo University (1995–2013).

Kazuaki Tanahashi (b. 1933) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Japanology who studied under Soichi Nakamura. He served as scholar-in-residence at San Francisco Zen Center (1977–1984) and is a fellow of the World Academy of Art and Science.

Kazufumi Oki (b. 1946) specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral coursework at Kyoto University and served at Shuchiin University as an assistant professor (attested 1982–1990) and professor emeritus (attested 2006–2013).

Kazuharu Mizuno (b. 1958) works in Tibetology and geography. He earned degrees from Nagoya University (BA), Hokkaido University (Master's), and Tokyo Metropolitan University (DSc), becoming a geography professor at Kyoto University around 2009.

Kazuhiko Atsumi (1928–2019) worked in philosophy and other fields. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1948–1954) and later held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1954–1989) and Suzuka University of Medical Science (~1991–1998).

Kazuhiko Yoshida (b. 1955) works in linguistics, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Sophia, Kyoto, Cornell (PhD under Jay Jasanoff), and Osaka universities. He held posts at Nagoya City Women's College and Nagoya City University (2021–2024).
Kazuhiro Kaneiwa is a scholar in Buddhist studies who held a post at Bukkyo University, attested in 2001 and 2013.

Kazuhiro Kawasaki (b. 1974) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his doctoral studies at Koyasan University, where he also held posts as a researcher (attested 2005) and special appointed professor (attested 2026).
Kazuhiro Yamamoto works in Indology and philosophy. He studied at Silpakorn University under doctoral supervisors Samniang Leurmsai and Chirapat Prapandvidya, attested in 2009.
Kazumi Yoshizaki works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. Yoshizaki studied at Toyo University and held a post at the National Museum of Ethnology (attested 2001).

Kazunobu Matsuda (b. 1955) specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Otani University under Shiro Matsumoto, and held posts as lecturer at Otani University and professor at Bukkyo University (1994, 2009, attested 2022–2024).

Kazuo Hyodo (b. 1948) is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Kyoto University and Otani University under Hajime Sakurabe, earning a PhD, and served as an assistant professor at Otani University (~1985–2014).

Kazuo Kano (b. 1974) works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. Educated at Kyoto University and the University of Hamburg (PhD), he has held posts at Hamburg, Kyoto University, Koyasan University, and Komazawa University.
Kazuo Matsumura (b. 1953) works in religious studies and Indology. He studied at Hitotsubashi University (~1972–1976) and held posts at Tenri University (~1986–1989) and Wako University (~2004–2018).

Kazuo Okabe (b. 1935) specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. Educated at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo, he held posts at the Institute for Zen Studies (1969) and Komazawa University (assistant professor 1973, professor 1979–2006).

Kazuo Osumi (b. 1933) is a scholar in Japanology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at the University of Tokyo (~1951–1964), he served as assistant professor at Hokkaido University (1964) and professor at Tokyo Woman's Christian University (1977–2001).
Kazuo Oyamada (b. 1952) specializes in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tamagawa University (~1971–1975) and held a post at Rissho University.
